patches.find: According to tradition, his crown came with him on the ship.

patches.replace: Omar se rio a su pesar

patches.replace: ¿Y qué le ve de malo? Pero si así lo canta

patches.find: Errors? But that's how
patches.replace: What's wrong with it, as you see it? But that's how

patches.find: Esa misma mañana, mientras vendía miel, empezó a decir
patches.replace: La mañana siguiente al incendio, mientras vendía miel, empezó a decir
patches.why: Unclear time reference: 'Esa misma mañana' follows two hypotheticals and has no antecedent morning; the rumour started the morning after the fire (cf. ña Gumersinda's 'a la mañana').

patches.find: That same morning, while he was selling syrup,
patches.replace: The morning after the fire, while he was selling syrup,
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: el asombro de quien descubre que lo habían juzgado de boca en boca
patches.replace: el asombro de quien descubre que lo han juzgado de boca en boca
patches.why: Tense sequence: generic present 'quien descubre' requires 'lo han juzgado', not the pluperfect.

patches.find: the astonishment of a man who discovers he had been tried by word of mouth
patches.replace: the astonishment of a man who discovers he has been tried by word of mouth
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: Ña Gumersinda se rió con toda la boca.
patches.replace: Ña Gumersinda se rio con toda la boca.
patches.why: Orthography: 'rio' (RAE 2010), site convention.

patches.find: Llevaba tres semanas escribiendo y borrando aquel párrafo
patches.replace: Llevaba días escribiendo y borrando aquel párrafo
patches.why: Repetition of 'tres semanas' in consecutive sentences; also she could hardly have drafted for the full three weeks when she 'tardó días en atreverse a escuchar' the recording.

patches.find: She had spent three weeks writing and deleting that paragraph
patches.replace: She had spent days writing and deleting that paragraph
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: En el colegio de Cartagena había aprendido a guardarse el palenquero
patches.replace: En sus primeros años en Cartagena había aprendido a guardarse el palenquero
patches.why: Logic: she left Palenque at seventeen (end of secondary schooling), so 'el colegio de Cartagena' contradicts the timeline.

patches.find: At secondary school in Cartagena she had learned
patches.replace: In her first years in Cartagena she had learned
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: El tío se rió por primera vez
patches.replace: El tío se rio por primera vez
patches.why: Orthography: 'rio' (RAE 2010), site convention.

patches.find: donde su tía abuela había vivido sola desde que volvió de Rusia,
patches.replace: donde su tía abuela, de vuelta de Rusia, había vivido sola desde que enterró a su madre,
patches.why: Plot logic: Nina came back in 1956 because her sick mother 'la reclamaba en cada carta', so she cannot have lived alone ever since she returned.

patches.find: where her great-aunt had lived alone ever since she came back from Russia,
patches.replace: where her great-aunt, back from Russia, had lived alone ever since she buried her mother,

patches.find: y en el acto se arrepintió de lo mucho que se parecía a la tía.
patches.replace: y en el acto se arrepintió del tono, que era clavado al de la tía.
patches.why: Logic: Nina is the one who kept doors shut, so 'regretting how much she resembled her' after saying she likes opening doors is contradictory; the resemblance is the curt tone.

patches.find: and instantly regretted how much she sounded like her aunt.
patches.replace: and instantly regretted her tone, which was her aunt's to a T.
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: La que fuera la casa de ambos durante casi veinte años,
patches.replace: La que fuera la casa de ambos durante tantos años,
patches.why: Plausibility: Liosha, 22 in 1956 and working in a factory, cannot have lived in a children's home for almost twenty years (many homes were also relocated during WWII).

patches.find: What had once been home to them both for almost twenty years,
patches.replace: What had once been home to them both for so many years,
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: La que fuera la casa de ambos durante casi veinte años,
patches.replace: La que fuera la casa de ambos durante tantos años,
patches.why: Card example kept verbatim with the story fix.

patches.find: What had once been home to them both for almost twenty years,

patches.find: Common error: using the past tense after por poco and changing the nuance (por poco tiró can mean 'she threw it away for a short time' in some contexts), or forgetting the subjunctive after por poco que.
patches.replace: The preterite (por poco se cayó) is also correct and common in the Americas, but never the subjunctive or the conditional. Common error: forgetting the subjunctive after por poco que.
patches.why: Wrong claim: por poco + preterite is standard (DPD/NGLE) and does not mean 'for a short time'; the card taught learners to avoid a correct form.

patches.find: Por poco for a near miss in the past takes the present indicative: por poco la tira.
patches.replace: Por poco for a near miss in the past normally takes the present indicative (por poco la tira); the subjunctive and conditional are wrong.
patches.why: 'why' overstated the rule (the preterite is also correct; it is simply not offered).

patches.find: "Hubo should be había"
patches.replace: "terminado should be terminada"
patches.why: Two correct answers: 'Había terminado la cinta y la puso otra vez' is also a valid correction; distractor replaced with a clearly wrong one.

patches.find: Eso pensé yo, y me pasé una semana juzgándola.
patches.replace: Yo pensé lo peor, y me pasé una semana juzgándola.
patches.why: Branch logic: replies 1 and 2 of the previous step ('no sacaría conclusiones', '¿tu familia nunca te habló…?') don't make 'Eso pensé yo' a sensible answer.

patches.find: That's what I thought, and I spent a week judging her.
patches.replace: I thought the worst, and I spent a week judging her.
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: por debajo del bajo y de las palmas sintéticas
patches.replace: detrás del bajo y de las palmas sintéticas
patches.why: Unhappy echo 'por debajo del bajo'.

patches.find: beneath the bass line and the synthetic handclaps
patches.replace: behind the bass line and the synthetic handclaps
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: Doña Eduviges Avalos, que hablaba
patches.replace: Doña Eduviges Ávalos, que hablaba
patches.why: Orthography: Ávalos is esdrújula and takes an accent.

patches.find: Doña Eduviges Avalos, who spoke
patches.replace: Doña Eduviges Ávalos, who spoke
patches.why: EN keeps the name spelling consistent.

patches.find: una licencia por cuatro cuartos
patches.replace: una licencia por cuatro soles
patches.why: 'Por cuatro cuartos' is a Peninsular idiom; Peruvian 'por cuatro soles' keeps the meaning in the story's dialect.

patches.find: «¿y si mandamos el video a la prensa, causa?»
patches.replace: «¿y si mandamos el video a la prensa? Un causa mío trabaja en un canal»
patches.why: Register slip: Yordi calls Zoila 'doctora' and 'causa' (bro) in the same message; 'causa' is kept (map dialect) as a noun for his friend.

patches.find: What if we send the video to the press, mate?
patches.replace: What if we send the video to the press? A mate of mine works at a TV channel.
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: exactamente donde la quebraba el muchacho de 1976
patches.replace: exactamente donde la quebraba el hombre de 1976
patches.why: Logic: in 1976 don Anselmo was 'unos cuarenta años', not a 'muchacho'.

patches.find: exactly where the young man of 1976 had broken it
patches.replace: exactly where the man of 1976 had broken it
patches.why: EN follows ES fix.

patches.find: con las gafas en la punta de la nariz
patches.replace: con los lentes en la punta de la nariz
patches.why: Dialect: Peru says 'lentes'/'anteojos'; 'gafas' is Peninsular.

patches.find: I hereby state, pursuant to the provisions of current copyright legislation, that my client considers the field recording in question to be in the public domain
patches.replace: My client hereby states, pursuant to the provisions of current copyright legislation, that the field recording in question is in the public domain
patches.why: EN mistranslation: the subject of 'manifiesta' is 'mi representada', not the lawyer.

patches.find: Folclor dicen. El panalivio
patches.replace: Los de la disquera dirán que es folclor. El panalivio

patches.find: Folklore, they say. My dad
patches.replace: The record people will say it's folklore. My dad

patches.find: si el permiso era solo para estudio, venderla en una canción
patches.replace: si el permiso era solo para estudio, vender la grabación en una canción

c2-06.grade: A : genuinely C2 (journalistic conditional, literary -ra/pretérito anterior, concessive conjecture all natural and repeated); the Cerralvo clue is planted in line 0 and paid off; décima quatrains scan as octosyllables with abba rhyme. Facts check out (renamed 1932; Cerralvo viceroy 1624–35; 'Ñanga' per INAH 2024; statue with machete)
issues_fixed: clumsy ellipsis 'otros más de una década más tarde'
EN dropped the hearsay of 'la corona habría llegado' (the topic being taught)
EN stranded relative clause in line 0
'rió' -> 'rio' x2 (RAE 2010, site convention)
card 4 circular wording ('twist… adding a twist')
role-play: step 1 answered '¿Errores?' after a reply that only proposed 'un pequeño ajuste'
issues_open: Plaque line 'El pueblo lleva su nombre desde 1932': 'su' can technically refer to 'los cimarrones'; acceptable on a plaque dedicated 'A Yanga', but 'el nombre de Yanga' would be fully clear (owner's call; gq6 option would need the same change)
Partner names Omar (c2-06) and Osmar (c2-07) are near-identical in neighbouring stories; consider renaming one
Jarocho/Mexican lexicon list from W8 notes (torito, develar, pásele/ándele) for a Veracruz speaker; whether Yanga's anniversary would have a son jarocho fandango with tarima

c2-07.grade: A : excellent C2 courtroom piece; the ndaje plot is airtight, the 'miel quemada' clue is planted (line 3), reused (line 8) and paid off (Toribio); the legal register and absolutes are idiomatic; mirative 'había sido' is attested for Paraguay (ra'e calque; RAE 2009; HAL hal-01330685)
issues_fixed: unanchored 'Esa misma mañana' (which morning?) -> the morning after the fire
tense sequence 'quien descubre que lo habían juzgado' -> 'lo han juzgado'
'rió' -> 'rio'
issues_open: 'señorías' in Villalba's closing line is the Spanish (Peninsular) form of address; Paraguayan courts more usually use 'Excelencias'/'señores miembros del Tribunal' – Paraguayan lawyer to confirm
All Guaraní lines (ndaje sentence, he'i chéve, iporã, aguyje, -na hyphenation) need a Guaraní speaker (W9 notes)
Procedure is stylised: reading a police statement aloud in an oral trial and having it 'ratified' would normally be restricted under the CPP (Ley 1286/98)
Whether the offence should be named 'testimonio falso' (Código Penal) rather than 'falso testimonio'

c2-08.grade: A- : moving, respectful, and the resolution is social as mapped; hedging/mood/conjecture topics are well demonstrated; risk lies in the unverified 'Ma' honorific, on which a card paragraph and gq item 7 depend
issues_fixed: 'tres semanas' repeated in consecutive sentences and at odds with 'tardó días en atreverse a escuchar'
timeline: 'el colegio de Cartagena' although she left Palenque at seventeen
'rió' -> 'rio'
issues_open: HIGH: 'Ma' as a title of respect before an older woman's name (Ma Petrona, Ma Cleotilde) could not be verified (web search finds only plural ma / ma-kuagro); if wrong, lines 0–12 names, card 1 sentence and gq7 must change – Palenquero teacher to confirm
'Kusungá' invented: confirm it means nothing unintended in Palenquero
Minor plausibility: Dorina heard the grandmother's long shout as a child yet never recognised the word; the story half-explains it ('sin preguntarse nunca qué decía'), acceptable as literary licence
Lumbalú/kuagro descriptions and the invented 'shout from the hill' custom: community reader for sensitivity

c2-09.grade: A : the strongest literary text of the set (free indirect speech, Asturian diminutive system, por poco family); the timeline arithmetic is correct and is the clue (1984 tape, 3-year-old in 1937, glass holder). Facts verified (El Musel 23–24 Sept 1937; Crimea Odessa→Valencia Sept 1956; 1956–59 expeditions)
issues_fixed: plot: Nina 'lived alone since she came back from Russia' though she returned to nurse her sick mother
illogical 'se arrepintió de lo mucho que se parecía a la tía' after saying she likes opening doors (Nina shut them)
implausible 'casa de ambos durante casi veinte años' (Liosha 22 and in a factory in 1956) – story + card example + EN
card 3 WRONG claim that por poco + preterite is an error meaning 'for a short time'
gq 'Hubo terminado…' had two correct answers ('Hubo should be había' is also a valid fix)
gq 'why' overstated the por poco rule
role-play: 'Eso pensé yo' did not follow two of the three previous replies
issues_open: 'ho' as a mother's vocative to her daughter, 'me presta', 'culinos', the invented Asturian lullaby line: Gijón speaker
A 3-year-old orphan evacuated in the care of a 14-year-old neighbour is plausible but at the young edge; historian may confirm
Celsa's 'vosotras… nosotros' (generic masculine for her own generation) – possibly 'nosotras'

c2-10.grade: A- : well-built legal comedy with a sharp ironic ending (the label copies the 'Corso' misspelling); all four topics demonstrated naturally; facts verified (RS 010-2009-MIMDES; Ley 28761; Zaña 2017); several dialect and logic slips fixed
issues_fixed: 'el muchacho de 1976' for a man of about forty
Peninsular items in Peruvian narration: 'por cuatro cuartos' -> 'por cuatro soles', 'gafas' -> 'lentes'
register clash: Yordi calls Zoila 'doctora' and 'causa' in one message
'por debajo del bajo' echo
'Avalos' -> 'Ávalos' (ES+EN)
EN mistranslation of the notarial letter (lawyer vs 'mi representada' as subject)
role-play: 'Folclor dicen' did not follow reply 0; 'venderla' without antecedent
issues_open: Timeline is very tight: song heard in May, 15-day deadline + extension, trip to Zaña, conciliation, settlement and press release all before 4 June – owner may want 'una tarde de abril' in line 0 (also check quiz/teaser)
'hoja de encargo' vs Peruvian 'carta de encargo'/'contrato de locación de servicios'; whether a performers'-rights dispute would go through 'audiencia de conciliación' (Peruvian IP lawyer)
Invented donation of Lindqvist's notebooks to the real Museo Afroperuano de Zaña: owner decision (could be a teacher note)
